summary.headline: Stove Kraft Q2 FY27 revenue rose 23.2% YoY to INR585 crore and EBITDA margin hit a record 12.9%, though exports lagged.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue was about INR585 crore (+23.2% YoY) with gross margin up 120 bps to 39.6% and EBITDA of INR75.3 crore (+32.7%, 12.9% margin). PAT rose to INR29 crore (+35.7%, 5% margin). H1 revenue reached INR1,065 crore (+30.8%) with H1 PAT of INR46 crore (+44.8%). Management attributed export softness to product changeovers and the IKEA ramp, and a rise in inventory and borrowings to a deliberate shift toward year-round manufacturing plus capex and China investment.

financial_highlights.change: +32.7% YoY vs INR56.8 crore; margin up 96 bps from 12%

segments.name: Induction cooktops
segments.commentary: Grew about 108% YoY in Q2 FY27; management says infrared and induction together will keep a higher baseline.

segments.name: Pressure cookers
segments.commentary: Grew 46.8% YoY, helped by demand after geopolitical disruption; inner-lid cooker business at Baddi is cited as fastest growing.

segments.name: Small appliances
segments.commentary: Grew 9.1% YoY in Q2; management says appliances are about 45% above base, and Black & Decker is being phased out.

segments.name: Pigeon (value brand)
segments.commentary: 3-year CAGR of 21%; 16 stores added across 9 cities in Q2, taking exclusive stores to 360.

segments.name: Gilma (premium brand)
segments.commentary: Relaunched in southern markets with 17 stores; running at about INR1 crore per month, D2C-led, target about 100 stores in 24 months.

segments.name: Channels
segments.commentary: General trade grew 52.2% and e-commerce 24.2% YoY; modern retail grew 11.9% in Q2 and 27.3% in H1; own retail grew 70.3% in H1.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue was flat-to-weak in Q2; about 11-12% of revenue on an annualised basis, with management targeting about 15% in 3-4 years.

guidance_outlook: Management expects about 30% growth in the near term; current growth is about 25%.
EBITDA margin ambition of 12-15% over the next 3-4 years; CFO-level guidance of 11-12% for FY27 per management's reply to an analyst.
Gross margin expansion of about 100 bps per year is being targeted, but management did not reaffirm it explicitly.
Capex for manufacturing kept below INR50 crore for the year; land and China investment (about INR100 crore combined including these) sit outside that.
Net debt-free status targeted soon; management says growth will not need additional working capital.
Exports expected to grow for the full year; IKEA and new products to ramp.
Existing facilities can support INR2,500-3,000 crore revenue before new capacity is needed.
capex_capacity: Baddi (Himachal) plant expansion for pressure cookers and small appliances, plus purchase of a ready factory building for immediate use.
Land adjacent to the factory, plus a KIADB (Bangalore) application and line acquisition; these are medium-term, with about 6-8 months to finalise.

China: investment capped at CNY20 million (about INR29-30 crore) across a trading WOS and a manufacturing JV step-down subsidiary; brownfield plant to make tri-ply clad discs, starting around end-December or early January.
Delhi facility: small investment to add appliance capacity; management expects capacity to be fully utilised before end of next year.
H1 cash-flow capex was about INR90 crore per management's figure cited by an analyst, with deferred payments affecting the cash line.
demand_pricing: Aluminium prices rose upwards of 50% and corrected about 10%; management says no meaningful cost relief yet and price hikes were taken over the prior 3-4 months with a lag.
Gross margin gain reflects price increases net of input cost inflation; management says it passes through input cost increases as a cost-plus company.
Shift from aluminium pressure cookers to stainless steel and tri-ply is underway; PTFE cookware demand faces negative consumer sentiment.
General trade growing about 50% in the last two quarters; management says unorganised players are hard to compete with given manufacturing and distribution scale.
Air purifiers launched in the last 2 months (imported, single model); chimneys manufactured in-house and growing.
Management says the Q2/Q3 seasonal margin premium over Q1/Q4 is about 0.5-1%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did exports underperform in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it exited some PTFE and ceramic cookware and the IKEA partnership was only just starting; export revenue was about 11-12% of annualised sales.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables, inventory and payables shift sharply, and why did borrowings rise?
qa_highlights.answer: A deliberate move to year-round manufacturing built inventory for Q2 and Q3; borrowings rose because of inventory, land, facility purchases and China investment, with positive cash flow expected by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Capex guidance for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Manufacturing capex stays below INR50 crore; land and China investments are outside this and together could be about INR100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why add capex now given capacity for INR2,500-3,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management framed capex as capability (China backward integration, cold spray plant) and small Baddi/Delhi additions, with growth running ahead of plan; it expects capacity fully used before end of next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise 43% in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail stores moved to franchise (commission-linked expenses up), with higher contract labour, power, fuel and freight, and job-work costs in H1 that management says will not recur.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins face pressure in Q4 and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 and Q3 carry a 0.5-1% margin premium over Q1 and Q4 due to operating leverage; sustained cost efficiency is the driver, with a 12-15% EBITDA margin ambition.

risks_watch: Export recovery: IKEA ramp and new cookware products need to deliver in Q3-Q4 FY27 given weak Q2.
Working capital and net debt: inventory build and borrowings rose; watch for the promised return to net-debt-free status.
Input cost: aluminium and copper volatility, with management saying pass-through is not automatic in the near term.
Gilma roll-out: 17 stores to a target of about 100 in 24 months, with heavy marketing investment at launch.
Other expenses and franchise shift: H1 other expenses rose about 43% (INR120 crore to INR180 crore), and management says this reverses in H2.
Appliance growth: small appliance growth of 9.1% and value-led ASP declines in kettles and air fryers; air purifiers are early and imported.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, margins and capital allocation, but evasive on specific numbers such as FY28 EBITDA and exact export guidance. Export underperformance and cash-flow movements were explained at length rather than quantified.
key_quotes: We are pleased to report a robust overall performance in Q2 FY27 despite persistent inflationary pressures and raw material cost volatility.
We are very confident of good growth in exports.
We are working towards getting to between 12% to 15%.

growth.why: Management expects about 30% near-term growth (current ~25%), backed by Baddi expansion, China tri-ply plant, Gilma/Pigeon store roll-out and price increases, though no order book is cited and existing facilities cover INR2,500-3,000 crore revenue before new capacity is needed.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin hit 12.9% (+96 bps YoY) and gross margin rose 120 bps to 39.6%, with management guiding Q2/Q3 seasonal premium of 0.5-1% and a 12-15% ambition over 3-4 years, though FY27 guide is only 11-12%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Baddi expansion and ready factory building targeted for Q1, China tri-ply brownfield plant starting end-December or early January (~INR29.5 crore), and Delhi appliance capacity expected fully utilised before end of next year; existing facilities still cover INR2,500-3,000 crore revenue.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects about 30% near-term growth versus current ~25%, backed by induction cooktops (+108% YoY), pressure cookers (+46.8%), general trade (+52.2%) and 16 Pigeon stores added in Q2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Land adjacent to factory, KIADB Bangalore application and line acquisition are medium-term with 6-8 months to finalise, and total land plus China spend could be around INR100 crore, so further capex disclosures are probable.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Growth running ~25% against a near-term ~30% expectation, but FY27 EBITDA guide of 11-12% is modest versus Q2's 12.9% margin and management was evasive on specific numbers.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Exports were flat-to-weak in Q2 (about 11-12% of revenue annualised), aluminium costs are volatile with no near-term pass-through relief, and export recovery depends on the IKEA ramp and new products in Q3-Q4.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: IKEA ramp and new cookware products are expected to ramp in H2, Gilma is expanding from 17 stores toward about 100 in 24 months, and air purifiers were launched in the last 2 months as an imported single model.

rows.label: Net debt-free status and working capital normalisation
rows.why: NWC days fell to 32 from 45 in Q1 and management targets positive cash flow and net-debt-free status by year-end, though borrowings rose on inventory, land and China investment.

rows.label: Other expenses reversal in H2
rows.why: H1 other expenses rose about 43% (INR120 crore to INR180 crore) from franchise shift, contract labour and freight, which management says will not recur.

rows.label: Export recovery via IKEA ramp
rows.why: Export revenue flat-to-weak in Q2 at about 11-12% of annualised revenue, with management targeting 15% share in 3-4 years and IKEA partnership only just starting.
